question: What is printed in the boxed bar on that staff?
note: Sean lost his place by voice; tile numbers below are matched to the pictures by content (our matching, confirmed with him tile by tile). His first 'tile 5' description is tile 7; his 'tile 7' description is tile 9; '4/8 notes', '2/8 notes', '3/16th' are voice-to-text for four eighth notes, two eighth [rests on the page], three sixteenths.

answers.1: a half note with ties on either side going to the measures on either side
answers.2: an eighth note rest followed by three unison eighth notes with stems going in both directions with beams on either ends
answers.3: two voices; top: an eighth note rest followed by three eighth notes, the first has a sharp, the second a natural sign; lower voice a whole note rest
answers.4: two voices; bottom a whole note rest; top: eighth note rest followed by three eighth notes, the second has a natural sign; a crescendo marking underneath
answers.5: the four eighth notes; the first two have the slur, the second two have the staccato markings
answers.6: unison half notes: a half note with stems going in both directions with a tremolo slash on either end
answers.7: a dotted quarter followed by a dotted eighth and three sixteenth notes; a slur from the previous bar lands on the dotted quarter; the dotted quarter has a tie to the dotted eighth; the three sixteenths have a slur over them into the next bar
answers.9: a G clef with a single flat; three eighth notes beamed together, two notes per stem (thirds), all staccato, accidentals on each (first: lower note sharp; second: lower natural; third: top note sharp); then a dotted quarter chord, the lower note has a flat, both tied into the next bar
answers.10: the eighth note chord, followed by 2/8 notes [as transcribed; two eighth rests stand there on the page], followed by a dotted quarter chord
answers.11: looks exactly like tile 7 [said 'tile five', his first label for that figure]
